OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to 
the passing away of Shri P.M. Sayeed , a Member of this House, on the 18 th 
December, 2005, at Seoul following cardiac arrest.   He was 65 years of age. 
Born at Androth Island, Lakshadweep, in May, 1941, Shri Sayeed 
had his education at the Government Arts College, Mangalore and Sidhartha 
College of Law, Mumbai. 
A lawyer, a political and social worker, Shri Sayeed devoted his life 
for the welfare of the poor and the downtrodden. He was associated with 
various social, welfare and cultural activ ities, particularly in Lakshadweep; 
and was instrumental in conducting inter-State cultural programmes and 
promoting folk arts of Lakshadweep. 
Shri Sayeed had a long and illustrious political career, which started 
with the membership of the Fourth L ok Sabha. He had the distinction of 
winning the Lok Sabha Election for ten times consecutively. He also served as 
Deputy Speaker of the Twelfth Lok Sa bha and the Thirteen th Lok Sabha. He 
was also Member of the Panel of Chairmen, Lok Sabha, from 1991 to 1992 
and 1996 to 1997. 
Shri Sayeed also served as the Un ion Minister of State and held the 
portfolios of Steel, Coal and Mines from 1979 to 1980; Home Affairs from 
1993 to 1995 and Information and Broadcasting from 1995 to 1996 and Union 
Minister of Power from May, 2004 till he breathed his last. 
Shri Sayeed was Chairman of  the Committee on Provision of 
Computers to Members of Parliamen t; Committee on Private Members' Bills 
and Resolutions, Lok Sabha; Committee on Budget of Lok Sabha; Library 
Committee and Joint Parliamentary Committee on Security Matters in 
Parliament Complex. He was also Secr etary and Deputy Chief Whip of the 
Congress Parliamentary Party. 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [19 December, 2005]  
Shri Sayeed represented the National Capital Territory of Delhi in 
this House from August, 2004 till date. 
A widely travelled person, Shri Sayeed visited many countries as a 
Member and Leader of various Parliamentary delegations. 
Shri Sayeed was a soft-spoken person and was highly respected. He 
endeared himself to one and all with his suave manners. 
In the passing away of Shri P.M. Sayeed, the country has lost an 
eminent Parliamentarian and an able administrator. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri P.M. Sayeed. 
I request Members to rise in thei r places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members 
of the bereaved family our deep sense of sorrow and sympathy. 
As a mark of respect in the memory of Shri Sayeed, a sitting 
Member, the House stands adjourned till 11.00 a.m. on Tuesday, the 2oth 
December, 2005. 
The House then adjourned at five minutes past eleven of the clock  
till eleven of the clock on Tuesday, the 20lh December, 2005.
